    Cross-universe transport of representation-finiteness #

    Finite-dimensional modules can be resized through Shrink. Combined with the idempotent characterization of indecomposability, this removes the same-universe restriction from transport of representation-finiteness across an algebra equivalence.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.idempotent_eq_zero_or_id_of_indecomposable_preadditive {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C] [CategoryTheory.IsIdempotentComplete C] {X : C} (hX : CategoryTheory.Indecomposable X) (p : X ⟶ X) (hp : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp p p = p) :
    p = 0 ∨ p = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id X

    In an idempotent-complete additive category, an indecomposable object's idempotent endomorphisms are trivial.

    An object with no nontrivial idempotent endomorphism is indecomposable, provided it is nonzero.

    CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M ↔ CategoryTheory.Indecomposable N

    Indecomposability of modules is invariant under a linear equivalence even when the module carriers live in different universes.
